claims.explanation: Clofibrate is a PPARα agonist that induces peroxisomal and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation genes; selective killing likely reflects dependence on PPARα-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming, with TP53 loss and intact PPARα signaling sensitizing lines, while RAS/BRAF-mutant or mesenchymal lines are protected. The strong enrichment of TP53 mutations among killed lines and the virtual-cell downregulation of mitochondrial metabolic genes (MPC2, DLD, TIMM9) support a metabolic-stress mechanism. Features predicting sensitivity include PPARA expression, TP53 mutation, and low dependence on the protected lineages' survival pathways.

PPARα/clofibrate induces mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase and ketogenesis
PPARα target cytochrome P450 fatty acid ω-hydroxylase induced by clofibrate
acyl-CoA synthetase required for fatty acid activation and PPARα ligand production
KRAS-mutant lines (pancreas, colorectal, ovary) are enriched among least affected
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines appear in both groups but several are least affected
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, seen in several protected lines
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK survival signaling in protected lines
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear among least affected (HCC4006, NCIH1648)
